sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: BharatRohan is not a pure drone-software exposure: agricultural output sales account for nearly two-thirds of FY26 revenue. Revenue tripled, but operating cash outflow widened sharply. FY26 PAT rose 12.1% against the original annual comparison or 37.9% against the prospectus-restated baseline; neither is equivalent to cash earnings. The calculated base return is 6.41% annually from the dated ₹95 observation, conditional on further financing. [S1] [S3] [S95]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: BharatRohan Airborne Innovations Limited, ISIN INE0QMV01017, BSE 544535. Annual report confirms BSE SME listing on 30 September 2025. Consolidated Indian accounting standards framework (Accounting Standards, not Ind AS), years ended March 2025 and March 2026. Review as of 20 October 2026; five-year horizon, 15% nominal hurdle, ₹5 lakh liquidity reference. [S1]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS4.38 and GQS4.40 have full canonical evidence-backed factor audits. IAS remains NS because funding/model confidence and executable liquidity are unresolved, not because all price evidence is absent. [S95]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Drone-based crop monitoring provides agricultural extension services. The same group sells agricultural inputs and outputs, including commodities. FY26 revenue comprises crop monitoring ₹25.7076 crore, agricultural outputs ₹56.1766 crore and inputs ₹3.5265 crore. Commodity procurement and inventory financing are economically distinct from recurring software revenue. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Hyperspectral monitoring and farmer relationships may improve crop decisions and procurement traceability. The annual report does not establish independently verified pricing power, customer retention, recurring contract duration or software-like marginal economics. Commodity execution and counterparty risk must not inherit a technology multiple merely because drones are used. [S1]

FY25 top-ten customer share42.84% improved from64.86% FY23; crop monitoring FY26₹25.7076cr remains meaningful despite commodity outputs₹56.1766cr. Annual report treats all activities as one reportable segment, so no separate technology margin is disclosed. Do not attach a software multiple to crop/commodity procurement. Prospectus explicitly identifies no directly comparable listed Indian company. Drone manufacturers are technology comparators but not working-capital matches; agricultural distributors are funding comparators but omit monitoring expertise. July17 board rescinded the direct US subsidiary plan and approved a proposed step-down entity under GroeiGids BV to market/package/sell spices, pulses and pantry staples. Incorporation and capital amount were not established by that proposal. This diversifies food-distribution exposure, not demonstrated drone revenue. [S1] [S2] [S4]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY26 consolidated revenue ₹85.4107 crore versus ₹28.1723 crore, +203.2%. Crop monitoring grew 82.9%, but agricultural outputs grew 326.6% and dominate the absolute addition. PAT ₹10.4593 crore versus original comparative ₹9.3297 crore is +12.1%, while comparison with restated FY25 ₹7.5864 crore gives +37.9%. Original comparative EPS ₹6.81 versus current ₹6.03 is diluted by the IPO and is not a like-for-like normalized earnings-growth measure. Prospectus history is FY23/FY24/FY25 revenue ₹6.4683/18.9549/28.1723 crore, PAT ₹1.8087/6.9040/7.5864 crore and CFO ₹0.7941/−8.1157/−3.8589 crore. The restatement bridge is explained under Financial Forensics, rather than silently splicing series. [S1] [S3]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The IPO raised ₹45.0432 crore gross and ₹39.7929 crore net per note 40. Of net proceeds, ₹27.3590 crore was used and ₹12.4339 crore remained earmarked, principally equipment and vehicles. Working-capital allocation ₹16.68 crore was fully used. Cash availability must be assessed after outstanding commitments, rather than treating all cash as surplus. [S1]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters Amandeep Panwar and Rishabh Choudhary each received ₹27.82 lakh remuneration versus ₹14.91 lakh previously. Note 42 lists ₹21.61 lakh advances to GroeiGids B.V. and a prior-year ₹109.66 lakh recovery from BharatRohan Innovation Foundation. Related parties are management-identified, relied upon by the auditor. These disclosures require transaction-purpose and recoverability review, not automatic governance reassurance. [S1]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 CFO was -₹27.7402 crore versus -₹3.2403 crore. Inventory absorbed ₹29.1583 crore and receivables ₹14.8034 crore. Two-year CFO/PAT is -1.565x. FY26 cash spending on PPE, intangibles and CWIP totals ₹7.4913 crore, giving an operating FCF proxy of -₹35.2315 crore. Closing inventory ₹44.0904 crore and receivables ₹24.7331 crore are substantial against ₹85.4107 crore annual sales. FY25 profit also benefited from negative tax expense ₹0.4952 crore and miscellaneous income ₹1.617 crore; normalize before comparing margins. [S1]

The apparent FY25 profit mismatch is substantially explained, not left as an automatic reliability failure. Prospectus AnnexureV starts from original audited PAT₹9.3297cr, deducts₹0.2060cr tax/MAT adjustment and₹1.6170cr restatement adjustment, adds₹0.0797cr deferred-tax adjustment, reaching₹7.5864cr. The₹1.6170cr miscellaneous-income benefit in the original annual comparison is therefore not normalized recurring growth. Cash-flow classifications also move noncurrent liabilities and tax items; the reported FY25 CFO figures remain separately labeled. Auditor relies on a separately audited Dutch subsidiary with only₹0.1051cr assets and nil revenue, not an unaudited material operating component. Edit-log reporting is positive. Mahveer Traders cheque/collection litigation₹0.2364602cr was recognized as bad debt/provision in FY26. These checks support ordinary governance rather than blanket reassurance or an unproven G2 fail. [S1] [S2] [S3]

FY26 inventory₹44.0904cr and receivables₹24.7331cr together equal80.58% of sales. Receivables₹19.2196cr are not due,₹1.0432cr less than six months overdue,₹4.0384cr six-to-twelve months and₹0.4319cr one-to-two years. No independently verified post-year recovery was available. Inventory realization is a commodity/quality/seasonality risk, not automatically obsolete stock. Core EBIT proxy=PBT+finance cost−other income:₹13.3389cr FY26 versus₹7.5795cr FY25. At assumed25% normalized tax NOPAT is₹10.0042cr versus₹5.6846cr. Invested-capital proxy equity+debt−cash is₹78.4261cr versus₹32.5036cr, including CWIP/development assets; average-capital ROIC≈18.04%, incremental NOPAT/incremental capital≈9.41%. Full cash exclusion is a favorable convention because IPO cash is earmarked; retaining earmarked cash in capital lowers returns. Neither proxy proves a mature cohort return. [S1] [S3]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Linked five-year operating/funding scenarios and18% FCFF cross-check are provided below. Dated secondary19October close95 permits conditional return sensitivities, not a live target or executable recommendation. [S1] [S3] [S95]

The attached annual model links revenue, EBIT, tax, working capital, capex, cash and debt. Bear/base/bull peak debt is₹18.23/20.64/14.96cr, versus₹3.9384cr starting debt, so even the base needs approximately₹16.70cr additional funding that has not been verified committed. End-year5 prices are₹19.94/129.59/356.26, giving15%-hurdle entry sensitivities₹9.91/64.43/177.13, conditional hurdle-entry values, not current executable targets. The18% FCFF cross-check gives₹8.46/56.45/156.47 per share. Low confidence is intentional: base margin compresses to12%, NWC falls from approximately78% toward60% of revenue, and terminal10× EBIT is an assumption, not a traded peer multiple. Funding failure invalidates those paths; it is not cured by an optimistic terminal price. Source-backed starting figures [S1] [S3]; all forward values are analyst assumptions.

BSE544535 issuer name agrees with BharatRohan; secondary19October OHLCV gives close95 and volume2400, with low=high=95. The228000rupee price×volume product is a provider-derived turnover proxy, not independently reported BSE traded value. Against95, the previously specified bear/base/bull terminal prices imply five-year CAGRs−26.82%/+6.41%/+30.26% approximately, with no dividends; calculate exact values in the linked model. Base is below the15% hurdle despite apparent terminal price upside. Funding failure, immature margins and inventory realization could invalidate every scenario. Missing quote is resolved only at secondary confidence; no automatic IAS upgrade. [S95]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Commodity inventory can lose value or take longer to sell, while receivables delay collection and new equipment consumes earmarked IPO cash. Further external capital could dilute shareholders even if reported revenue grows. Drone technology alone does not protect agricultural commodity realization. [S1]

A20% inventory loss is₹8.8181cr before tax,84.31% of FY26 PAT; a30-day receivables extension requires₹7.0201cr cash. Base-model terminal multiple±2× changes the15%-hurdle entry value by approximately₹12.85 per share. A20% increase in terminal shares without compensating earnings/cash reduces every terminal per-share value by16.67%; this is dilution sensitivity, not a funded issuance model. A lender limit below the base peak₹20.64cr would require equity, asset realization, slower growth or default-risk mitigation, so no assumption of unlimited credit is presented as feasibility. Five-times and ten-times price paths require37.97% and58.49% annual returns, respectively; no scenario probabilities are assigned; executable liquidity and funding remain unverified. [S1]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold price gains require 37.97% and 58.49% annualized returns over five years. At the dated ₹95 close and unchanged 1.992302 crore shares, fivefold price at an assumed 15× exit P/E requires ₹63.09 crore PAT; tenfold requires ₹126.18 crore, versus FY26 ₹10.4593 crore. At an illustrative 10% net margin, the former needs about ₹630.9 crore revenue plus funded working capital. These are reverse hurdles, not a forecast or evidence that a technology premium is justified. Sustainable per-share cash earnings must establish the path. [S1] [S3] [S95]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track inventory realization and ageing, crop-monitoring receivable collections, segment margins, remaining IPO deployment ₹12.4339 crore, advances to foreign subsidiaries, tax disputes and fully diluted shares. Direct-tax contingent liability rose to ₹1.4511 crore from ₹0.0022 crore; indirect-tax exposure is ₹0.0524 crore. [S1]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved funding and implementation confidence. The applicable business, forensic and linked-model review is complete, but the low-confidence funding assumptions prevent numeric IAS or an executable recommendation. The dated secondary quote is sufficient for conditional valuation arithmetic; a primary-only quote rule is not the reason for the hold.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Annual primary filing and issuer version, final prospectus/restatement/concentration, current board updates and BSE listing notice reviewed. Secondary OHLCV supplies a dated price sensitivity; no claim of official traded value or surveillance clearance. [S1] [S2] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S6] [S95]

GOV.reason: Audited edit-log controls and recognition of a disputed debt are positive; transparent revised subsidiary plan is preferable to an unexplained scope change. Contrary: management-identified related parties and new foreign food-retail allocation need continuing scrutiny; limited listed record prevents a high score.

MOAT.reason: Specialized monitoring expertise and wider customer base are useful, but commodity majority and no demonstrated segment pricing power imply contestable economics. Contrary: monitoring growth82.9% is genuine adoption, not evidence of no differentiation.

REV.reason: Strong monitoring growth and diversification support demand, but commodity turnover dominates absolute growth and EPS falls. Contrary: growth is not exclusively low-value trading, so a bottom-end score would ignore service expansion.

DUR.reason: Precision-agriculture services and broader customers provide an accessible runway; US food-retail proposal adds execution/funding rather than proven technology runway. Contrary: deployment and customer acquisition already occurred, so opportunity is not entirely speculative.

CAP.reason: CWIP-inclusive invested-capital growth outpaces incremental after-tax operating profit; estimated incremental return9.4% is below the assumed14–18% capital hurdle. Contrary: average-capital ROIC proxy18.0% and immature new equipment leave room for improvement.

CASH.reason: Three consecutive negative-CFO years across reviewed scopes plus inventory/receivable absorption support persistent poor realization. Contrary: FY23 CFOpositive and FY26 debtors mostly not due; losses/defaults are not presumed.

BAL.reason: Low current financial debt and large equity support resilience, but earmarked cash and operating burn require external-funding stress. Contrary: no current insolvency inferred and negative CFO is not the same as a maturity default.

EXEC.reason: Monitoring revenue and IPO deployment show delivery; weak collections and unproven foreign retail diversification prevent a strong execution score. Contrary: service growth argues against treating all new initiatives as failed.

EARN.reason: Revenue growth converts weakly into per-share profit and cash, with commodity mix and prior tax/restatement effects. Contrary: FY26 still generates positive operating earnings and monitoring growth; not a loss-making core by assumption.
